replacementEvidence: generated-assets-2026-09-04.json records eight new landing-v3 illustrations. Their exact byte hashes, prompts and provider output-rights basis are now registered in assets.json and openai-output-rights-basis-2026-09-05.md. This is provenance documentation, not legal signoff. note:
Git introduction records establish repository history only. They do not prove authorship, provider terms, stock-media permissions, or trademark rights. These records intentionally are not accepted asset declarations.

2026-09-10: every pattern below was re-checked BY HASH against the two records written since, and the 39 DISTINCT files they expand to are covered — 23 by the project owner's 2026-09-05 confirmation and 16 by assets.json as AI-generated. (The patterns produce 49 hits because public/landing-v3/* recurses into its gen/ and usecases/ subdirectories; 39 is the file count, and 23 + 16 = 39 is the coverage. This line said 26 until 2026-09-19, which double-counted.), each with a generator, a stated rights basis and evidence. Nothing was outstanding; this file had simply not been re-read since those records were written, which is the failure it now exists to prevent rather than repeat.

The patterns are KEPT rather than deleted. They are what scripts/asset-provenance-coverage.test.mjs watches: a new file under any of them whose hash is in neither record fails the build. That forward guard is the point — public/landing-v3/ is exactly where a stock image would land and look ordinary.

Still not asserted here: trademark, and whether the owner confirmation or the provider output-rights basis is sufficient for any particular use. Those are unchanged and unsigned.

2026-09-19: nine of these hashes were computed over a CRLF working copy instead of the committed bytes, so they described no file in the repository and the gate's verdict depended on core.autocrlf. Both records were corrected to the committing blobs (`git cat-file -p <commit>:<path>`), and both suites now hash the committed bytes. The files themselves did not change: each one is byte-identical to its committing commit, all of which predate the confirmation.
